themes.name: Home as a Place
themes.description: Rooms, houses, neighborhoods, landscapes, and the sensory details of dwelling.
archaeology_questions: What survives online after a physical place changes or disappears?
Which details did the crawler preserve that an official history might miss?

themes.name: Migration, Borders, and Displacement
themes.description: Leaving, arriving, exile, forced movement, and rebuilding a sense of home.
archaeology_questions: How does a captured web page preserve a moment between departure and arrival?
What context about movement and borders is absent from the archived fragment?

themes.name: Family, Ancestry, and Inheritance
themes.description: Family memory, ancestors, intergenerational stories, heritage, and inherited identity.
archaeology_questions: How do private memories become public digital artifacts?
Which family histories survive because somebody once put them on a web page?

themes.name: Language and Cultural Belonging
themes.description: Mother tongues, translation, cultural memory, and belonging expressed through language.
archaeology_questions: What changes when an archived story is translated?
What can wording, dialect, or code-switching tell us that metadata cannot?

themes.name: Housing, Homelessness, and Precarity
themes.description: Unstable shelter, eviction, housing insecurity, homelessness, and the politics of dwelling.
archaeology_questions: Whose housing experiences are easiest to lose from the public web?
Does the archive preserve testimony while erasing the conditions around it?

themes.name: Exile, Return, and Nostalgia
themes.description: Longing for a place, returning home, homesickness, and homes transformed by memory.
archaeology_questions: Can an old capture preserve a version of home that no longer exists?
How does the date of capture complicate the date remembered by the writer?

themes.name: Objects, Food, and Rituals
themes.description: Everyday objects, meals, customs, sounds, and rituals that make belonging tangible.
archaeology_questions: Why do small domestic details survive when broader context disappears?
What can ordinary objects reveal about a vanished online community?

themes.name: Chosen Family and Community
themes.description: Friendship, solidarity, adopted communities, and belonging created outside inherited ties.
archaeology_questions: How does a surviving fragment reveal the shape of a community around it?
Which relationships become invisible when links and comment threads vanish?

themes.name: The Internet as Home
themes.description: Blogs, forums, social networks, fandoms, games, and other digital places of belonging.
archaeology_questions: Can an abandoned website still be a home?
What did the crawler capture of the community, and what lived outside the page?

themes.name: Lost and Inaccessible Places
themes.description: Demolished homes, inaccessible homelands, environmental loss, and places reachable only through memory.
archaeology_questions: What does a digital trace preserve after access to a place is lost?
How should we talk about absence without pretending the archive is complete?

themes.name: Identity and Contested Belonging
themes.description: National, local, racial, religious, gendered, and other identities shaped by inclusion or exclusion.
archaeology_questions: Who was able to describe belonging publicly on the web represented by this crawl?
What identities are flattened by extraction, classification, or translation?

themes.name: Memory, Forgetting, and the Archive
themes.description: Remembering, forgetting, unreliable memory, missing context, and the accidental survival of digital traces.
archaeology_questions: Why did this fragment survive?
What cannot be responsibly reconstructed from the captured text?
